newsitem.title: FINLAND: Enso sees Holtzmann op profit down in '97.
newsitem.headline: Enso sees Holtzmann op profit down in '97.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group Enso Oy said on Monday it expected the operating profit at German E.Holtzmann, in which it has bought a majority stake, to fall this year along with paper prices.
"Last year, (Holtzmann) was very profitable and it will be profitable this year too but, with the general trend, at a lower level," Enso's CEO Jukka Harmala told a news conference.
"(Operating profit) will fall this year along with falling paper prices," said Magnus Diesen, Enso head of corporate planning, referring to Holtzmann.
Despite this, acquiring Holtzmann would have a positive effect on group earnings per share this year, Harmala said.
"We have calculated it will have a mildly positive impact on the earnings per share ratio," Harmala said.
"Above all, it will raise cash-flow per share," he added.
Holtzmann's 1996 operating profit was about 580 million markka with net sales around 2.46 million markka, Enso said.
Enso said earlier it would buy a 50.4 percent stake in Holtzmann for 1.8 billion markka and planned to buy the rest.

Harmala said Enso had an agreement with Holtzmann's owner Westdeutche Allgemeine Zeitung to buy 39 percent more for the same price per share in 1998, and that it might buy the final 10 percent held by private owners but had no redemption obligation.
"The remaining 39 percent are based on the same pricing ...it is based on the same price per share," Harmala said.
The German group has over 500 million German marks in liquid assets and no interest-bearing debt, Harmala said.
